From ea55c65dedf40e9c1911dc1e63e26bc9a59692b9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Jun 2024 12:56:33 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] serial: bcm63xx-uart: fix tx after conversion to
 uart_port_tx_limited()

When bcm63xx-uart was converted to uart_port_tx_limited(), it implicitly
added a call to stop_tx(). This causes garbage to be put out on the
serial console. To fix this, pass UART_TX_NOSTOP in flags, and manually
call stop_tx() ourselves analogue to how a similar issue was fixed in
commit 7be50f2e8f20 ("serial: mxs-auart: fix tx").

Fixes: d11cc8c3c4b6 ("tty: serial: use uart_port_tx_limited()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Brown <doug@schmorgal.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240606195632.173255-4-doug@schmorgal.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c b/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
index 34801a6f300b..b88cc28c94e3 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
@@ -308,8 +308,8 @@ static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_MCTL_REG);
 	val = (val & UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_MASK) >> UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_SHIFT;
-
-	pending = uart_port_tx_limited(port, ch, port->fifosize - val,
+	pending = uart_port_tx_limited_flags(port, ch, UART_TX_NOSTOP,
+		port->fifosize - val,
 		true,
 		bcm_uart_writel(port, ch, UART_FIFO_REG),
 		({}));
@@ -320,6 +320,9 @@ static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_IR_REG);
 	val &= ~UART_TX_INT_MASK;
 	bcm_uart_writel(port, val, UART_IR_REG);
+
+	if (uart_tx_stopped(port))
+		bcm_uart_stop_tx(port);
 }
 
 /*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c`**
   - The function `bcm_uart_do_tx` was modified to change the way transmission is handled.
   - The call to `uart_port_tx_limited()` was replaced with `uart_port_tx_limited_flags()`, passing `UART_TX_NOSTOP` as a flag.
   - A manual call to `bcm_uart_stop_tx(port)` was added to ensure that transmission is stopped if it is currently halted.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change from `uart_port_tx_limited()` to `uart_port_tx_limited_flags()` addresses an issue introduced in a previous commit where the implicit call to `stop_tx()` led to garbage output on the serial console. By passing `UART_TX_NOSTOP`, the patch prevents the automatic stopping of transmission, which was causing the problem.
- The addition of the manual call to `bcm_uart_stop_tx(port)` ensures that the transmission can still be stopped when necessary, maintaining control over the transmission process while fixing the bug related to unintended stopping. This modification is analogous to a similar fix applied in a previous commit for a different driver.

 uart_port_tx_limited()

When bcm63xx-uart was converted to uart_port_tx_limited(), it implicitly
added a call to stop_tx(). This causes garbage to be put out on the
serial console. To fix this, pass UART_TX_NOSTOP in flags, and manually
call stop_tx() ourselves analogue to how a similar issue was fixed in
commit 7be50f2e8f20 ("serial: mxs-auart: fix tx").

Fixes: d11cc8c3c4b6 ("tty: serial: use uart_port_tx_limited()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Brown <doug@schmorgal.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240606195632.173255-4-doug@schmorgal.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the implicit call to `stop_tx()` that was introduced when the `bcm63xx-uart` driver was converted to use `uart_port_tx_limited()`. This led to the transmission being stopped unexpectedly, resulting in garbage data being sent to the serial console. The fix involved passing `UART_TX_NOSTOP` to prevent this automatic stopping and manually controlling the stopping of transmission when necessary.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 {
 	unsigned int val;
 	bool pending;
 	u8 ch;
 
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_MCTL_REG);
 	val = (val & UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_MASK) >> UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_SHIFT;
-
-	pending = uart_port_tx_limited(port, ch, port->fifosize - val,
+	pending = uart_port_tx_limited_flags(port, ch, UART_TX_NOSTOP,
+		port->fifosize - val,
 		true,
 		bcm_uart_writel(port, ch, UART_FIFO_REG),
 		({}));
 	if (pending)
 		return;
 
 	/* nothing to send, disable transmit interrupt */
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_IR_REG);
 	val &= ~UART_TX_INT_MASK;
 	bcm_uart_writel(port, val, UART_IR_REG);
+
+	if (uart_tx_stopped(port))
+		bcm_uart_stop_tx(port);
 }
